citations.context: Like, for example, in some cultures, when you greet people, you greet them with a handshake, others with a hug, others with a kiss. Great greet the brothers with a holy kiss, says Paul, right? The relative part of that is how to do it, but the fact you ought to greet people is consistent. All right. And we cut we unpack this a lot, and I don't have enough faith to be an atheist. C. S. Lewis did some amazing work in his small book called The Abolition of Man, where he points out that regardless of what culture you're talking about, that cultures agree at their core on certain moral principles.
citations.creator: cross-examined
citations.title: If a Culture Accepts Cannibalism Does That Make It Right?
